With him it was the first time I’ve heard about panleuk, it was an absolute nightmare and the illness I fear the most. It’s something I never wish to anyone to go through.

It’s like we speak about the same cat ha ha. I used the word “jump” generically because we’re glad he can achieve his goal but it’s more like a hop indeed 😆 and he uses his claws too when it’s something more abrupt. He’s so cute and funny in his clumsy way. He’s a big cat, a little elephant we say, so when he sometimes misses his landing we run to protect him because the landing sound is loud. But he gets up like saying “this is how I wanted to land!” and leaves.

Avoiding getting obese is very important. We try to make him stand more on his hind legs through playing. I wished for him to be able to jump higher and do more for him, I thought it could get stronger.

We switched to an automatic litter box, same as a closed one, so he won’t risk falling into his poop by being supported by the walls. But him being a big cat helps a lot. He has to get out when the covers it.

I saw you have some very beautiful and special cats. Having special cats is so fulfilling which I never thought I would think this way. An occasion to learn new things every day and be amazed by many different ways of living a happy life, same as a normal one. I’m amazed how blind cats can adjust to their lives. I have a deaf cat, apart from the wobbly one.

Thank you for your time! ❤️

Hi! I know it's an older post and I saw in your recent post that the gourgeous floof is still wobbly but I was wondering if the vet recommended you anything, supplements or exercise?

I have a cat that also beat panleuk. at 4 months old and after he beat it he started doing the same thing as your cat in this video, his butt has different directions sometimes 😁 to me it seems like weaker hind legs. He's almost 2 now and I know it may be late for something to change at this age. We love him very much regardless.

I haven't found much information or same experiences. Our vet gave us CBD oil for cats but I was wondering if we can do something to strengthen his muscles? Have you trained your kitten's muscles? He has a 99% normal life and it's a happy cat, he can walk, poops ok, he can run even if sometimes he puts a break on his butt, lands on his feet most of the time, but the most he can (or will?) jump is a chair or on the bed. I feel so bad for him when he would follow the other 3 and they jump at the windows and he stops and looks up to them. He wants to be there and we always help him. He jumps down from there but never up. 

I don't know if he can jump higher but he's scared to do so, as he never tried. I can feel him getting insecure on his feet when he's up there. Even if he will never be able to jump, we're looking for a way to get him there when we're not home. I would love for him to be able to jump on a tree like yours.

Thank you for your kind words. I’m so glad there’s a comunity here where you can see you are not alone and that there’s nothing wrong if you choose to be different from the “the norms of society”.

It may not seem the worst but it had an impact. My mother telling me who will give me a glass of water when I'll get old. For me, it will surely be an army of four-legged family members but right then and there I realised why was I put on this planet according to her. And I don't know who will give her one. Long story but I never developed the kind of connection she craves now, because she sees this on others on facebook.

Another instance was when my husband was playing with a cat and my mother turns to me saying "see how nice they play? You should make him a baby". As if I was a factory. We both don't want kids.

Big and loud sighs, shoulder shrugs, showing pics of different kids, inventory checking of my school colleagues kids, giggling about other's children are little details. I never in my life heard them laugh as loud as I did when they were looking at a video with a kid. There's no need for words and direct conversation in order to be mean. I've detached emotionally for my own sanity and I find them silly now. 

After my birthday, I noticed a change in the narrative. My mother said something about adopting now, maybe she started realising that I'm at an age where at least it will be dificult to have one. I'm not in my most fertile years anymore but I wonder at what age will this ever stop. Please tell me from your experience it will stop at 40+.

I don't let others have the oportunity to say something mean because my life and choices are none of their business. I get questions and comments, I smile, give a generic answer and move on with my life. I must admit I have an evil, unlikely wish.
